name: reversible-door
statement: Among open options pick the one from which the others stay additive: refuse a form not yet admitted rather than admit it, and keep admitting a form already admitted rather than restrict it.

counter_examples.why: Refuses comparison chains that ran, the one-way tightening of an admitted form, because their verdict differed from the binary twin.
Makes programs that print correct values today raise NameError, restricting admitted behaviour to remove an order-dependent value (T1).
Picks (a), stated as one-way in practice, over (b) from which (a) was additive, to keep one narrowing rule.
Chooses a one-way output change (Python's evaluation order) over the reversible deviation row.
Promotes identity-before-__eq__ in containers, one-way for output, over recording a deviation.
Adopts Python truthiness for T | None, one-way for output, over refusing or the spec's null check.
Ships a new public Core type for every open mode (stated one-way) rather than the deviation subset.
Implements dataclass copy(), one-way once called, rather than rewriting the docs that promise it.
Emulates Python's run-time UnboundLocalError instead of the compile-time refusal the applied default had.
Refuses 1e400 (Python's inf) although python3 runs it; the door argument is used against the Python value, not for admission.

boundary: Yields when the reversible option leaves a silent difference from Python on a COMPARED surface, a silently wrong or order-dependent value (T1), or withdraws a documented surface; then the one-way fix is taken and recorded by direction.
gap: No written law says which door to prefer; FS only says the fidelity aperture opens by ruling. The 'a refusal can be relaxed later' reasoning appears in about 70 rows but in no law.

name: uniform-verdict-across-forms
statement: A desugared form, an alternative spelling, another host, or another member of an operator or declaration family gets exactly its primitive's verdict, value and diagnostic code; no form-specific refusal or exemption.

counter_examples.why: After R-ER made the two match-guard positions alike for truthiness, R-EU makes them differ for narrowing; uniformity is by mechanism (what gates the whole arm), not by syntactic position.
Accepts two spellings (caps and verbatim) for one CLR enum member, to keep running programs.
A bool needle is refused for bytes while R-NW admits an int needle, though Python's bool is an int; the family is drawn by Sharpy's conversion rules, not Python's.
Int-backed enums follow plain Enum for == but IntEnum for ordering (R-OW): one type, two flavours across one operator family.

boundary: Uniformity is judged by Sharpy's own type and conversion rules and by the mechanism (what gates, what converts), not by Python's family lines; a second spelling may survive to keep a correct program running (T3).
gap: N7 covers reads of one name by spelling and T4 covers module/class/generic hosts; neither extends to desugared forms (chains, augmented operators, pipes), builtin versus user types, or declaration kinds sharing a convention.

name: one-authority-per-fact
statement: Each fact or behaviour has one implementation every consumer calls: a compile-time check calls the runtime's pure function, an operator and its library function share one engine, and one authority spells each name or identity.
gap: CR2 and VC11 make the emitter pure and facts materialized once, but say nothing about runtime/compile-time twins or shared engines; mirrors were twice built and retired (R-BX, R-CG).

name: csharp-limit-named-refusal
statement: When C# cannot express a construct, refuse it before Roslyn with a named Sharpy code and the steer a C# programmer would write; do not emulate it with a lowering users could depend on.

counter_examples.why: Emulates CPython's value-before-target evaluation order with a hoist instead of inheriting C#'s order.
Emulates Python's UnboundLocalError with a compiler-emitted assigned flag instead of refusing.
Emulates a mutable dataclass default through a nullable constructor parameter plus ??, a sentinel C# consumers see.

boundary: Emulation is taken when the lowering is unobservable from Sharpy (R-AV) or when refusing would leave ordinary Python programs either refused en masse or printing a different value (R-QL, R-AI).
gap: A1, T2 and RR imply refusal over a raw C# error, but none requires a named code with a C#-idiomatic steer, and RR's 'zero-cost bridge' does not say that a costly or depended-on emulation is the one-way door to avoid.

name: no-invented-type-or-conversion
statement: The compiler never invents a type or conversion: a common type is the slot's or an operand's own; anything beyond value-preserving widening is spelled by the user; disagreeing candidates are refused, asking for an annotation.

counter_examples.why: Inside a narrowing a store of the payload type is implicitly re-wrapped into T?, though R-G says T? converts implicitly in no direction.
A nullability-oblivious CLR reference is used directly as T with an inserted boundary check, an implicit conversion by design (platform types).
A loose T | None flows into a plain T with a compiler-inserted check and a warning rather than a required spelled conversion.

boundary: Compile-time constants that fit the target, stores into a narrowed Optional, and nullability-oblivious foreign values convert implicitly; everything else is spelled.
gap: A3 and AP ('no magic') say types are static and None is opted into, but not that inference may only pick a stated type or that narrowing conversions must be spelled.

name: diagnostic-code-per-cure
statement: A diagnostic code means one failure with one cure: reuse it, naming the kind in the message, for the same mistake; mint a new code when the cure differs; never filter a code by route.
gap: CR10 requires an explanation for every code but does not say when to mint versus reuse a code, nor 'one mistake, one diagnostic'.

name: silent-wrong-first
statement: A group that removes a silently wrong value is queued ahead of groups fixing refusals, crashes or tooling; tooling and tests-only residues wait behind user-facing silent-wrong work, regressions excepted.

counter_examples.why: The owner moved user-facing language features ahead of deeper correctness work, saying recent plans were not user facing.
A user-facing feature group was pulled forward ('we should not hold it off') over the preferred order.
Three silent-wrong rows were left allowlisted to wait for their class fix.

boundary: Order applies within a band; across arcs the owner weighs user-facing value, and a silent-wrong cell waits when its class fix is already scheduled.
nearest_written_law: batch-issues SKILL step 3 (not a listed law)
gap: The skill gives the band order but not the residue cap (R-GF) nor when user-facing features outrank it (R-PM).

name: group-by-class-and-seam
statement: Cells join the open tracker and group whose contract owns their class; defects on one seam form one group with one generator, built by the group that consumes it.

counter_examples.why: Forms a new residue group instead of distributing to trackers, unlike R-JW.

boundary: A new group is formed when the cure reuses facts a just-landed group built (R-JY); otherwise cells go to existing trackers (R-JW).
gap: VC1, VC10, VC11 and CR13 nearly state it; missing is the new-group-versus-existing-tracker test.

name: collision-is-error
statement: When two declarations, imports or source files claim one name in one scope, refuse and name both; neither order, kind nor star-ness picks a silent winner, and no deterministic rename is applied.

counter_examples.why: A user module shadows a same-named CLR namespace with a warning, not an error.
A local module shadows stdlib, referenced libraries and CLR namespaces with a warning, as Python's sys.path order.

boundary: When the other party is an open-ended external set (CLR namespaces, references), whose growth would newly refuse existing code, the local name wins with a default-on warning naming the escape.
gap: N2 refuses a read whose meaning differs by reading order; it does not cover declaration, import or file collisions, nor the open-external-set exception.

name: tooling-keeps-user-bytes
statement: An editor, formatter or refactoring route keeps the user's written spelling and bytes unless it can prove the change legal and meaning-preserving; it re-spells only when forced, and otherwise is not offered.

counter_examples.why: The formatter collapses runs of blank lines to one rather than preserving the layout as written.

boundary: A formatter run the user asked for may canonicalize within a stated bound (R-ET); repair routes acting on an unparseable document may not.
gap: No written law covers tooling output; this is new.

name: promote-fidelity-where-exact
statement: Promote a Python surface to COMPARED by whole type or message family, covering what .NET reproduces exactly or Core alone can cure; the remainder becomes one family deviation row.

counter_examples.why: The defaultdict factory keeps a fixed placeholder as a deviation, while R-CJ later compares every Stdlib repr with Python.

boundary: Where an exact reproduction would rewrite genuine values (R-NS, R-FL's 128+N), the inexact part stays a deviation even inside a promoted family.
gap: FS says promotion is by owner ruling naming a family, but gives no criterion; the rows apply 'exact on .NET or Core-only cure' every time.

name: measure-before-mechanism
statement: Add a mechanism, optimisation, CI leg or runtime-target move only after a measurement shows the need; record an unmeasured hazard. Performance is reported for the owner to judge, not gated automatically.

counter_examples.why: Adds a per-OS CI leg without a measured failure, because one platform is not a control for another.

boundary: Correctness checks on every platform the product ships for are not optional.
gap: VC5 makes measurements carry a sha; no law says to measure before building a mechanism.

name: documented-surface-implemented
statement: A documented feature that can be typed and lowered is implemented rather than documented away; the spec is rewritten only where the feature has no CLR carrier or admitting it would be the one-way door.

counter_examples.why: Deletes the spec section on named parameters in function types instead of implementing it.
Replaces the spec's null-check truthiness rule with Python's, rewriting the spec to the ruling.
Rejects the spec's per-class .NET exception bridge and rewrites the spec.

boundary: The spec yields when it promises something with no CLR carrier (R-BR) or when a later principle (Python fidelity, R-OB) supersedes its text by ruling.
gap: CR7 says change the implementation, never the spec, with no exception; the owner amends the spec by ruling in several rows, so CR7 needs its exception path stated.

name: loose-none-fails-like-python
statement: A possibly-None `T | None` operand in an operation Python accepts stays legal, warns, and fails as CPython does; a literal None where the type cannot hold None is a compile error.

counter_examples.why: Its first form refused ordering on T | None at compile time; the later principle allowed it with a warning, so the same case was decided both ways.
Refused == None on a CLR reference with an `is None` steer; lifted later by R-ES.

boundary: Applies to the loose `T | None` spelling only; Sharpy's strict `T?` is refused until narrowed. It overrides T2 for that spelling.
gap: T2 prefers a compile error over a run-time error with no carve-out; the loose-None rule chooses the run-time TypeError plus a warning, and T2 does not say so.

name: untypeable-api-is-deviation
statement: A Python library surface that cannot be typed statically, or whose Python value occurs only in misuse, becomes one recorded deviation row with a steer, not dynamic invocation, generated factories or a widened nullable type.

counter_examples.why: open accepts every Python mode with a new Core type rather than a deviation for the binary/update subset.
int byte/bit methods are added because a 'not provided' row is sound only with an alternative route.

boundary: A typeable surface with no other route is implemented; only untypeable, misuse-only, or alternative-covered surfaces deviate.
gap: FS says where a divergence is recorded, not which surfaces may diverge; AP forbids 'because Python has it' without the typeable/alternative test.

name: land-semantics-before-instruments
statement: Do not build an instrument, generator or stopgap on semantics a ruled change will flip; land the semantic change first, and move an existing structure intact before redesigning it.

counter_examples.why: An instrument blind spot is drained before the silent-wrong band it audits.

boundary: An instrument that hides missing refusals goes first, since the band it audits depends on it.
gap: VC11 orders generators before hand matrices but not semantics before instruments.

name: coverage-over-ci-capacity
statement: Coverage a contract requires is kept and CI capacity raised to carry it; every known failure is a counted, cited row, and a missing precondition reports Skipped, never a vacuous pass.
gap: VC2 and the gap-discovery contracts cover cited allowlist rows; the rule that CI capacity grows rather than coverage shrinks is unwritten.

name: clr-values-keep-clr-shape
statement: A CLR value keeps its CLR identity and nullability-oblivious shape; Sharpy may add capabilities but never subtracts what the CLR shape shows, and converts it only explicitly or with a check at a declared boundary.

counter_examples.why: PascalCase CLR member spellings on a Sharpy builtin receiver are refused, subtracting a CLR capability.
str.upper(...) through the CLR-backed builtin type name is refused like a user class.

boundary: Builtin types that are Sharpy types over a CLR backing follow Sharpy rules; the principle covers foreign values only.
gap: CV ('wrap .NET, expose Python') governs Core/Stdlib APIs; it is silent on foreign CLR values flowing into Sharpy code.

name: repr-is-construction-spelling
statement: A value's str/repr is its source construction spelling with payload reprs; where the runtime lacks the source information, print a fixed documented placeholder, never CLR text or compiler-injected names.

counter_examples.why: Every Stdlib repr is COMPARED with Python, which a defaultdict placeholder (R-BN) does not meet.

boundary: A placeholder is a deviation only until a cheap mechanism carries the information (R-DG); then the name is kept.
gap: FS's str/repr row says 'COMPARED as ruled' and lists rulings, without the rule they share.

name: one-mechanical-name-rule
statement: Name mangling is one mechanical rule for every name; exceptions are spelled with the backtick escape and collisions it creates are refused, never handled by tables, per-name renames or silent fallbacks.

counter_examples.why: The module-class merge special case (a class named like its file) is kept because it is a closed one-way door for C# consumers.
CLR enum members resolve by caps and by verbatim spelling.

boundary: A special case already visible to C# consumers is not reopened (R-AD).
gap: AP's 'no magic' and the name_mangling spec do not state the escape-over-table rule or collision refusal.

name: host-invariant-output
statement: A program's verdict and output never depend on the machine: locale, filesystem case, or assemblies a process happened to load; an OS that cannot reproduce a behaviour gets its own deviation row.

counter_examples.why: strftime %Z uses the libc name on Unix and the .NET display name on Windows, a per-OS split.

boundary: Where an OS lacks the data (Windows time-zone names), the difference is confined to that OS and recorded.
gap: T4's 'host' means module, class or generic class, not operating system or machine; FS covers culture only.

name: sentinel-defaults-not-magic
statement: A Python default or calling convention C# cannot express is modelled by overloads, a nullable parameter with a body coalesce, or a lambda steer; never an in-band magic value or dynamic invocation.

counter_examples.why: User def defaults that C# cannot hold are refused with a steer, while R-EV gives library functions overloads; forward overloads are recorded as future for user code.

boundary: Overloads are synthesized only at rung 1 in library source; user-written defaults are refused with a steer.
gap: AP forbids magic but does not name the replacement mechanisms or where each applies.

name: identity-never-runs-user-code
statement: `is` is identity only and never runs user code or a type test; `==` always runs the type's declared equality and is refused when none is declared; enum members count as identities.

counter_examples.why: Containers check identity before __eq__ for reference elements, so `in` and container == can skip the declared equality.

boundary: Container search follows CPython's documented identity-first semantics (R-PL); value-type operands of `is` answer False with a warning.
gap: No written law; the rule lives in rulings and the spec.

name: contained-fix-ships-now
statement: A contained fix to a false refusal or crash on an ordinary program, with a closed matrix and no seam an in-flight group owns, ships now as a chore, not with its distant group.

counter_examples.why: A rare crash waits for its scheduled group because the ruled lowering there would rewrite any stopgap.
A refusal is not relaxed now because a scheduled change would re-tighten it.
Cells join their class group rather than carving seams out of its contract to land sooner.

boundary: Not when a scheduled ruled fix would rewrite the interim change, or when the fix carves a seam out of another group's contract.
gap: CLAUDE.md allows no-plan PRs for contained band bugs and CR13 limits chores to seam-free work, but neither says when to pull a fix forward.

name: pre-1.0-break-early
statement: Before 1.0 there is no compatibility promise: breaking respellings land early, unconsumed public APIs that cannot be made correct are deleted, stale hand models are dropped, and ruled designs ship without a feature flag.

counter_examples.why: A naming design visible to C# consumers is treated as a closed one-way door and not reopened.
A deviation is kept to avoid making the C# consumer surface ambiguous, treating it as a one-way change.

boundary: Rows disagree on whether the C# consumer surface is protected before 1.0; R-GW and R-KM say no users exist, R-AD and R-EW protect it.
gap: No written stability policy; the clash over the C# consumer surface needs a ruling.

name: process-extensions-are-one-off
statement: An extension of a process limit (an extra verify pass, a raised ratchet pin) is granted once on the owner's quoted word and is never precedent.

counter_examples.why: A fifth verify pass is allowed on another plan; with R-NY, R-OR and R-QC, extensions recur, so the two-pass cap is routinely exceeded by request.

boundary: None stated; recurrence suggests the cap itself needs a written extension clause.
gap: VC12's convergence rule and R-LW's two-pass cap have no extension clause, so every extension is asked.

name: clr-limit-saturates-not-refuses
statement: A run-time argument Python accepts but a CLR limit cannot hold saturates, or raises CPython's nearest exception, recorded as one family deviation row; the call is not refused.

counter_examples.why: A numeric literal out of its type's range is refused at compile time, not saturated to inf as Python would give.
A non-zero decimal literal that underflows to zero is refused rather than saturating to zero.

boundary: Values in source text, known at compile time, are refused (T2); only run-time values saturate. R-FH calls refusing Python-accepted calls the one-way option, R-HU calls admitting Python's value the one-way option: the door reading flips with compile-time knowability.
gap: A1 inherits numeric width and FS routes divergences to the ledger, but neither says to saturate rather than raise or refuse.

name: bug-dependent-program-not-correct
statement: Under T3, a program whose current value comes from a defect, or whose verdict differs from its primitive twin's, is not a correct program; changing it needs a direction record, not a deviation row.

counter_examples.why: Int-backed enum ordering keeps .NET order as the status quo, a recorded deviation, rather than refusing as Python's Enum.

boundary: Status-quo behaviour that is consistent and documented (R-OW) is kept as a deviation, not treated as a bug.
gap: T3 does not define 'correct'; rows treat bug-dependent and twin-divergent programs as not correct.

name: tier-below-letters-at-charter
statement: A group's tier may be set below its derived letter at charter time when full-tier dimensions have no subject (tests-only, mechanical respellings); once planning begins tiers only rise.
gap: VC12 lists when a group is full and forbids lowering after implementation begins, but gives no criterion for overriding a derived full letter to light.

name: static-check-only-definite
statement: A static check refuses only a definite mismatch; where the operand kind, format spec or target symbol is not statically known, it stays silent and the run-time check answers.

counter_examples.why: Deletes a lossy-CLR-mapping decline so every CLR overload refusal is explained; possibly the opposite of R-U's 'oblivious where the bridge cannot map' (not confirmed beyond the row text).

boundary: Holds where the missing fact is unknowable at compile time; T2 governs wherever the fact is known.
gap: T2 prefers compile errors but does not say the checker must not guess when facts are missing.

name: users-first-release
statement: A defect that breaks the documented install on a supported host is fixed at once as its own chore and released as a patch, and a known workaround is posted on the issue immediately.
gap: New.

name: backed-enum-flavour
statement: A backed enum behaves as the Python enum flavour of its backing (IntEnum, StrEnum) for every operator.

counter_examples.why: Cross-type == on int-backed enums answers False (plain Enum), not by value as IntEnum would.
Ordering on a string-backed enum is refused (plain Enum), while R-QG compares string-backed == by value (StrEnum).

boundary: No consistent boundary: string-backed enums are StrEnum for == and Enum for ordering, int-backed the reverse. R-PK's reason ('no .NET order to keep') suggests 'keep .NET behaviour where it exists, else refuse', which R-ON does not fit.
gap: No law picks an enum flavour; this is a clash for the owner to rule, not a principle ready to write.

notes: Ungrouped rows are mostly one-off scheduling placements (group order, lane order) and single-case cli/process choices with no reusable principle. Scope has no tooling value; editor/formatter principles are filed as 'diagnostics'. Main clashes: reversible-door vs csharp-limit-named-refusal/loose-none on whether to refuse or emulate when Python runs the program (R-AI, R-QL, R-OP); clr-limit-saturates (R-FH: refusing is the one-way door) vs reversible-door (R-HU, R-IA: admitting is the one-way door), split by compile-time knowability; silent-wrong-first vs R-PM/R-GX user-facing-first; pre-1.0-break-early vs R-AD/R-EW protecting the C# surface; backed-enum-flavour has no consistent principle (R-ON, R-OW, R-PK, R-QG); documented-surface-implemented vs CR7's no-exception wording; R-HH vs R-HT treat a spec-silent 'runs vs refused' surface as COMPARED and DEVIATION respectively. R-U vs R-AT is flagged from row text only and is unconfirmed. Members are 'confirmed or plausible'; only ids in 'checked' were read in all-rows.md.
